title: Launch readiness: audit schemata & exception workflow
content:
Purpose:
This working checklist captures the security gating activities required before a production launch that touches RBAC v2, audit logging schema changes, automated evidence collection, and SIEM export pipelines. It is intended for release engineers, security reviewers, and SREs to validate compliance evidence and approve exceptions when necessary.

Scope:
- Changes to RBAC v2 role mappings, policy enforcement paths, or directory sync behavior.
- Any modifications to audit log schema (new fields, renamed fields, retention policy changes).
- New/updated evidence automation that gathers release artifacts (evidence bundles, proof bundles).
- SIEM export changes (endpoints, format, encryption, routing rules).

Preconditions (must be completed before review):
- Feature branch merged to release candidate and deployed to staging with feature flags turned on for a canary tenant.
- Automated test run that validates RBAC role checks exists and passes (unit + integration).
- Schema migration plan documented with backward-compatibility analysis.
- Evidence automation job defined and run successfully at least once with synthetic data.
- SIEM sink acceptance test executed (end-to-end) and sample events observed.

Checklist: RBAC v2
1) Role & Permission Review:
   - Confirm all new roles are documented with intent, owners, least-privilege justification.
   - Verify role-to-resource mappings are explicit (no wildcard rules unless justified).
   - Ensure separation-of-duty and approval paths are enforced for sensitive roles (admin, auditor, infra-deploy).
   - Check for default-allow policies; convert to explicit-allow where possible.

2) Directory & Sync Behavior:
   - Validate SCIM / IdP sync rules will not unexpectedly add privileged users.
   - Confirm group-based roles are handled consistently across accounts/tenants.

3) Test Coverage & Incident Simulation:
   - Unit tests for policy evaluation logic added.
   - Integration test that exercises both allow/deny paths for each role change.
   - Short chaos test: revoke a role and assert app behaviour degrades to safe failure (no silent data exposure).

Checklist: Audit log schema
1) Schema Contract:
   - List of schema changes with field names, types, and descriptions included (field-level doc).
   - Back-compat plan: field deprecations, mapping plan, and migration window defined.

2) Mandatory Fields Verification:
   - Ensure each auth-related event includes: event_id, timestamp (RFC3339), actor_id, actor_source, action, resource_id, resource_type, outcome, request_id, trace_id, and origin_region.
   - New fields must include a version tag in the envelope (audit_schema_version).

3) Retention & PII Handling:
   - Retention window and archival process documented (who, where, how long).
   - PII fields identified; ensure redaction/encryption in transit and at rest.

4) Producer Contracts and Validation:
   - Producers must validate payloads against the schema at produce time.
   - A schema-validator lambda/job exists; successful run documented in evidence.

Checklist: Evidence automation & packaging
1) Evidence Bundle Contents:
   - Deployment manifests (k8s manifests, docker image digests).
   - RBAC diff: before/after snapshots of roles and bindings (timestamped).
   - Audit log sample slices covering the deployment window (min 1 hour pre/post).
   - SIEM export sample showing event ingestion and mapping.
   - Automated test run logs (unit/integration/siem tests).
   - Checklist of reviewers and signoffs (with timestamps).

2) Automation Run Requirements:
   - Evidence automation must be runnable end-to-end from a documented command or CI job.
   - Output bundle must be immutable (artifact in object storage with digest) and linkable from the release ticket.

3) Evidence Freshness & Tamper Resistance:
   - Evidence must include cryptographic hashes of key artifacts and a signed manifest of what was collected.
   - Retain provenance: who triggered automation, job id, and commit SHA.

Checklist: SIEM export & ingestion
1) Export Endpoints and Formats:
   - Supported formats enumerated (ndjson, syslog RFC5424, Kafka topic + schema).
   - TLS enforced for transport; mutual TLS where available for on-prem sinks.

2) Field Mapping & Enrichment:
   - Ensure audit schema fields map to SIEM parsable fields; provide parsers/observability rules.
   - Confirm any enrichment (geo, user agent parsing) happens post-ingest with documented logic.

3) Monitoring & Alerting:
   - Alert if export delivery latency spikes or error rate > threshold for 10m.
   - Healthcheck endpoints exist and are scraped by prometheus with dashboards linked.

Sign-off matrix (required for greenpath):
- Engineering owner: name & timestamp
- Security reviewer (sec-owner): name & timestamp
- SRE oncall signoff for observability/export: name & timestamp
- Product/PM ack (for risk acceptance): name & timestamp
- Compliance representative (if regulated customer impact): name & timestamp

Exception request flow (if a gating item fails):
1) Submit exception: SEC-EXC-<yyyy>-<seq> ticket created with: failing item, impact analysis, mitigation controls, expiration window, and owner.
2) Triage: security leads + eng owner decide accept/reject within 48 business hours.
3) Temporary controls required for approved exceptions:
   - Compensating control list (increased logging, narrowed blast radius, manual approvers).
   - Short TTL (max 30 days) unless extended with documented review.
4) Evidence for exceptions:
   - Capture proof of applied compensating control (config diffs, screenshots, alert rules created).

Rollforward & rollback guidance:
- If post-launch telemetry shows elevated security errors or SIEM ingest failures, trigger rollback plan in infra runbook.
- Maintain a rollback artifact set (previous image digests, previous RBAC snapshot) accessible from the release ticket.

Notes & common pitfalls observed in prior launches:
- Silent schema changes cause downstream SIEM pipelines to drop events (validate with sample consumers).
- Defaulted allow policies creeping in via group sync rules — always test with a staging identity provider.
- Evidence bundles missing producer metadata (who/when/how) reduce audit value.

Required artifacts for acceptance (attach to release ticket):
- RBAC delta file (rbac-delta-<release>.json)
- Audit schema diff and validator run output (schema-diff.txt, validator.log)
- Evidence automation artifact URL (s3://redwood-evidence/<release>/) with manifest and checksums
- SIEM export acceptance test output and sample events (siem-sample-<release>.ndjson)
- Sign-off snapshot (signed manifest or google doc with explicit signers)

Reviewer guidance and templates:
- Quick triage checklist template (copy/paste into ticket):
   - Does change introduce new privileged role? Y/N
   - Any schema field renamed/removed? Y/N
   - Evidence automation ran successfully? Y/N
   - SIEM consumer validated? Y/N
   - Compensating controls required? Y/N

- Exception approval template fields (to include in SEC-EXC):
   - Item failing gate, rationale, mitigations, expiration, monitoring hooks, rollback plan, approvers.

Next steps & ownership:
- Security owner (Avery Chen) will run the first formal review for this release; escalate unresolved items to Security Director.
- Engineering owners to attach all artifacts and confirm tests in staging prior to review meeting.

Appendix: quick references
- RBAC v2 design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Sec/RBACv2-Design
- Audit schema registry: https://schemas.redwood-internal/api/audit/v1
- Evidence automation job: infra-ci/expose-evidence-job (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1842)

This document is a working checklist — expect iterative updates. Keep evidence links in the release ticket and reference SEC-EXC tickets for exceptions.
